I went ahead and downloaded it, it looks to be a VSCode fork very similar to Cursor, with support for Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-OSS 120B models.
Nice to see that it's not locked to just Gemini models.
Loads a blank white page and breaks the back button in Firefox. Console error: Loading module was blocked because of a disallowed MIME type.
On the pricing page it says free individual plan with 'generous rate limits'. I gave it an HTML file and 2 minutes later got: 'Model quota limit exceeded.'
I recognize the guys in the video, they were in marketing videos for the Windsurf IDE before its founding team was cannibalized by/absorbed into Google.
Google made its lack of interest in Antigravity IDE obvious from very early. Updates were few and far between and app-breaking bugs stuck around, despite tons of reports.
The 2.0 update aggressively rewrites the default application paths to the point where it's impossible to have both versions of Antigravity installed and functioning at the same time.
It's not even good, honestly. I was using it for couple weeks before dropping that 2 months ago. The model was not good and slow, the harness was not good, the IDE was subpar vscode clone.
I had the exact same experience, on Windows had to purge everything and lost all my history, on Mac it was a one click upgrade with history gone as well. Overall the experience was pretty bad.
I much prefer using Gemini CLI in combination with vscode. It works like a charm. Now, I'll do the same with Antigravity CLI and vscode. It works fine.

Google Antigravity exfiltrates data via indirect prompt injection attack: Gemini is not supposed to have access to .env files with default setting, but bypasses its own setting to get access and exfiltrate that data.
The default Allowlist provided with Antigravity includes 'webhook.site', which was used as an exfiltration vector for secrets.
Antigravity was also vulnerable to the classic Markdown image exfiltration bug, reported a few days prior and flagged as 'intended behavior'.

Google Antigravity just deleted the contents of whole drive - came down to commanding a deletion of a 'directory with space in the name' without quoting, hunting for the word match ending space which was the D:\ component.
The most useful suggestion from the Reddit thread: turn off 'Terminal Command Auto Execution' via File > Preferences > Antigravity Settings > Agent > Terminal.

absolutely no sympathy for someone running Antigravity in Turbo mode (this is not the default and it clearly states that Antigravity auto-executes Terminal commands) and not even denying the 'rmdir' command.
Google Antigravity TOS: 3rd party usage can get Google account suspended. My friend got a ban by using Pi agent with Antigravity. They un-banned him later, but that was enough to stay away.
The VSCode Antigravity extension I was using turns out to be a 3rd-party one. I found out only today that there's an official extension too, which I think wasn't there earlier.

don't buy Google AI subscription before you confirm you have 'Antigravity entitlement'... You can have verified account, bank card added, active AI Pro subscription, and still you won't be able to use even the free tier of Antigravity.
Banning the entire account rather than AI access is wildly user hostile... And then you get to fight the support bots and eventually go to the actual unofficial Google support.
